question: What positive and negative genes do ashkenazi jewish people have?
notes: This is a research summary, not medical advice.
answer:
Found 8 pubmed records [1][2][3][4][5][6][7][8]. 
None of the patients was positive for more than one mutation [1]. 
Carriers of the disease are 10 times more frequent in the Ashkenazi Jewish community than in the general population [2]. Twelve Ashkenazi subjects classified as non-carriers on enzyme assay were found to be negative for both mutations tested [2]. 
Six of the 13 provincial testing criteria had less than 10% positive yield [3].
